holidays.name: Darwin Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of science and reason honoring the birthday of Charles Darwin, with lectures, museum events, and plenty of people gleefully pondering finches and barnacles.
holidays.origin: Charles Darwin was born on February 12, 1809. Darwin Day events began in the 1990s, after which the Darwin Day movement grew into an international observance championed by science and humanist groups.
holidays.funFact: Darwin was born on the exact same day as Abraham Lincoln, February 12, 1809, and he spent eight years studying barnacles alone.

holidays.name: Lost Penny Day
holidays.description: A day to acknowledge the humble penny by picking up stray coins you find, treating each as a tiny gift from the universe, and perhaps contemplating whether pennies should still exist.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to Abraham Lincoln's birthday, since his portrait appears on the U.S. penny, which has carried his image since 1909. It is an unofficial, grassroots observance.
holidays.funFact: The Lincoln penny was the first circulating U.S. coin to feature a real person, and it debuted in 1909 to mark the 100th anniversary of his birth.

holidays.name: Plum Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the rich, boozy, steamed dessert that contains no plums whatsoever. Time to set something on fire for dessert and call it tradition.
holidays.origin: Plum pudding comes from medieval England, where 'plum' was a general term for dried fruits like raisins and prunes. The pudding became closely tied to Christmas, and this unofficial food day gives it a second chance in February.
holidays.funFact: Traditional recipes often have a coin hidden inside, and in Victorian times finding it was thought to bring luck to the diner.

holidays.name: National Freedom to Marry Day
holidays.description: An awareness observance recognizing the right of couples to marry and to have that choice honored equally, often marked with rallies, weddings, and educational events.
holidays.origin: It was started in 2004 by Evan Wolfson and the Freedom to Marry organization, and it is held on the Saturday before Valentine's Day rather than a fixed date.
holidays.funFact: The date was originally held around Valentine's Day to link the cause to romance, making it one of the few awareness days that doubles as a very large wedding invitation.

holidays.name: Sculpture Appreciation Day?
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek reminder to stop and admire the statues, busts, and chiseled lumps in your life and pose awkwardly next to them for photos.
holidays.origin: This is an informal social media era observance, popular with museums, art lovers, and local park enthusiasts who like to celebrate public art.
holidays.funFact: Michelangelo reportedly said that every block of stone has a statue inside it, and it is the sculptor's job to discover it.
